executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveal a multi-threat landscape across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) in the Americas represents the highest-priority zoonotic threat, with ongoing animal detections and human spillover risk flagged in multiple PAHO updates through March 2026. Mpox continues to circulate in the Americas region, and dengue transmission remains hyperendemic across Latin America and the Caribbean. Additional concerns include resurgent measles, pertussis, yellow fever, hantavirus, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season in April 2026.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) zoonotic spillover risk and concurrent resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases across the Americas represent the most urgent public health priorities requiring immediate coordinated response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing circulation in animal reservoirs
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans flagged; BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential
Sustained transmission in poultry and wild birds creating persistent human exposure opportunities
Cross-species detections reported across the Americas region
threats.action: Activate enhanced surveillance for human cases, enforce strict biosafety protocols at animal-human interfaces, pre-position antivirals, and coordinate with FAO/OIE on wildlife and poultry outbreak containment

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating active circulation
BSL-3 select agent requiring heightened biosafety and case management protocols
Continued community transmission in multiple Americas countries
Risk of importation to European and other regions given international travel
threats.action: Enhance contact tracing, expand vaccination coverage for at-risk populations, ensure BSL-3 laboratory capacity for diagnostics, and issue travel health advisories

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 indicating hyperendemic transmission
Multiple serotypes circulating simultaneously increasing severe disease risk
Early 2026 case counts consistent with or exceeding prior high-burden years
Vector control capacity strained across multiple affected nations
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations, enhance severe dengue case management capacity, accelerate dengue vaccine rollout where approved, and issue regional health alert

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 indicating active transmission risk
BSL-3 pathogen with high case fatality rate in unvaccinated populations
Epizootics in non-human primates serving as sentinel events for human spillover risk
Vaccination coverage gaps in endemic and at-risk areas
threats.action: Urgently assess vaccination coverage gaps, deploy emergency vaccine campaigns in affected areas, strengthen primate surveillance as early warning system, and enforce vaccination requirements for travelers

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026 indicating active outbreak activity
Measles elimination status threatened in multiple countries
Vaccination coverage gaps exacerbated by COVID-19 pandemic disruptions still not fully recovered
Cross-border spread risk given high transmissibility (R0 12-18)
threats.action: Conduct urgent vaccination coverage assessment, implement catch-up immunization campaigns targeting under-vaccinated cohorts, strengthen outbreak response capacity, and enhance measles surveillance sensitivity

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained elevated incidence
Resurgence pattern observed across multiple countries simultaneously
Infants under 6 months at highest mortality risk
Waning immunity in adolescents and adults fueling transmission chains
threats.action: Review and strengthen maternal Tdap vaccination programs, ensure infant vaccination schedule adherence, enhance laboratory diagnostic capacity, and investigate potential pathogen evolution affecting vaccine effectiveness

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
threats.pathogen: Sin Nombre virus / Andes virus (Hantavirus spp.)
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert December 2025 indicating case clusters
High case fatality rate (35-50%) with no approved antiviral treatment
Rodent reservoir activity potentially elevated due to environmental conditions
Person-to-person transmission risk with Andes virus variant
threats.action: Enhance rodent surveillance and control in affected areas, strengthen clinical recognition and early supportive care protocols, investigate environmental drivers of increased rodent-human contact, and issue public health advisories for high-risk occupational groups

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza (Southern Hemisphere Season)
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Concurrent RSV circulation noted in January 2026 alert indicating dual respiratory pathogen burden
Simultaneous circulation of influenza and RSV straining healthcare capacity
Seasonal transition period creating surveillance gaps for novel influenza variants
threats.action: Accelerate Southern Hemisphere influenza vaccination campaigns, enhance influenza-like illness surveillance, ensure antiviral stockpiles are adequate, and monitor for any antigenic drift or unusual severity signals

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3/BSL-4 select agents have been identified in active circulation: (1) Avian Influenza A(H5N1) - a BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential, flagged in two PAHO updates (November 2025, March 2026) with ongoing zoonotic transmission risk across the Americas; (2) Monkeypox virus (MPXV) - a BSL-3 select agent, flagged in a PAHO update (April 2026) with active community transmission in the Americas. Yellow fever virus, while a BSL-3 pathogen, was also flagged via alert in March 2026. These detections collectively warrant heightened biosafety vigilance, enhanced laboratory containment protocols, and prioritized public health response resources.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific reports identified in surveillance titles; however, Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance is an emerging global concern relevant to the pertussis resurgence flagged in multiple PAHO reports
Influenza antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) monitoring is critical given H5N1 activity and seasonal influenza co-circulation
Broad-spectrum antibiotic overuse during dengue misdiagnosis episodes risks selecting for resistant gram-negative organisms in endemic regions
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous resurgence of multiple vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis, yellow fever) across the Americas suggests persistent post-pandemic immunization gaps that have not been fully addressed
Co-circulation of H5N1 in animal reservoirs alongside active seasonal influenza creates conditions favorable for reassortment events with pandemic potential
Dual respiratory pathogen burden (influenza + RSV) observed in January 2026 may recur in the Southern Hemisphere winter season starting April-May 2026
ECDC issued five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) suggesting sustained elevated threat activity in the EU/EEA
Geographic clustering of arboviral threats (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in the Americas reflects expanding Aedes mosquito vector ranges potentially linked to climate-driven habitat shifts
Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) and GLP-1 medication misuse alert (February 2026) indicate growing non-infectious public health threats requiring integrated surveillance systems
